caption: Type while a menu is open: rows filter at once, the first match is highlighted, empty groups hide.
↑ ↓ move the highlight, Enter picks, Esc or a click outside closes; the caret returns and nothing moved.
A new page: the caret is in a faint “Untitled”; Enter moves to a first line that hints “Press / for blocks”.
Type “## ” at the start of a line: it becomes Heading 2 at once. Ctrl+Z gives back the typed characters.
**word** or Ctrl+B makes bold in place; *word* or Ctrl+I italic; Ctrl+U underline.
The / menu is one list: Basic blocks first, Study folded at its end. Typing finds any command by name.
Typing “scr” finds Scripture though Study is folded. The same list in a narrow pane and a floating tab.
A Scripture block: typing a book completes it (“josh” → Joshua), so the name and numbers cannot be wrong; the verse previews under the field.
Several verses and ranges across chapters: Num 25:18–26:1 is one block, each verse with its reference.
Drag one Scripture block beside another: they sit side by side to compare.
In a list: Enter makes a new item, Tab indents, Shift+Tab outdents, Enter on an empty item leaves the list.
Click the triangle (or Ctrl+Enter): the toggle folds and unfolds; a heading can be a toggle. Kept as <details>.
Select text: a bar appears above it. On scripture in a page it adds Mark and Margin note.
Mark ▾ on scripture in a page: the Legend's styles; the mark is the reader's mark, on the same words.
Mark, step 1: select words of scripture in a page. The selection bar shows Mark and Margin note.
Mark, step 2: Mark ▾ opens the Legend's styles, searchable.
Mark, step 3: pick Zeal. The words take its style in the page at once.
Mark, step 4: it is the reader's mark. Open Numbers 25 and the same words carry Zeal.
Margin note from a page: select scripture, Margin note; the note is written in that verse's margin and shows in the reader.
@ then a reference: the verse is placed as a link chip with its reference.
Click the chip: a popup with the verse. Drag it by its grip anywhere; Esc closes it and the page is as it was.
Whole chapter: the popup grows to Psalm 106, scrolled to verse 30 and marked; it can still be dragged.
Open beside: the passage goes to the side reader at Psalm 106:30; the page stays; Back returns.
Hover a block: + and the grip appear in the gutter. The text does not move.
What + and the grip do: + adds a line below (Alt+click above); the grip drags the block, or opens its menu when clicked.
Click +: a new empty line below, with the / menu already open.
Drag the grip: a blue line shows where the block lands; dropping moves it.
Click the grip: the block menu, searchable, with Edited and the word count at its foot.
Turn into ▸ Heading 2: the block changes kind and keeps its text.
Duplicate (Ctrl+D): a copy appears right below the block, with the caret in it.
Copy link to block: a link to a place in a page. It does not replace scripture references, which stay references and are found by the page index.
Move to: choose a page; the block leaves this page and is last in the chosen one.
Delete (or Del on a selected block): it goes, and “Deleted · Undo” offers the page's Undo.
Several blocks: drag across, Shift+click or Esc; a pale wash on each; the grip menu acts on all.
Drag in the margin to select several blocks: a pale band follows the pointer; every block it touches is selected.
/callout in the / menu makes a callout; its kinds are Question, Answered, Key point and Note.
Click a callout's icon: its kind menu. A Question becomes Answered, and back.
Today's pages: `> [!question]` and `> [!done]` show as Question and Answered; the questions list finds them.
A callout holds several lines and a nested list.
In the questions list the callout shows its first line, its page and its kind; the rest opens with the page.
Color ▾ on selected words: 8 plain colors and Default, for emphasis only. Text color means nothing; marks carry meaning.
A folder's color is the only organizing color: pick it from the folder colors; its pages show the dot by the title and in the side list.
Edit anything: “Edited just now” in quiet gray, later “Edited 2m ago”. There is no Save button.
The page's three dots: one searchable menu, with Edited and the word count at the foot.
Appearance ▸ Serif (or Small text, Full width, Table of contents): the page changes at once.
Appearance › Table of contents: an outline of the page's headings folds beside a long page; click one to go there.
Lock page: a quiet lock in the bar, no handle, and typing does nothing.
Copy contents: the page's Markdown, with scripture expanded verbatim from the database.
Ctrl+K preview of a page with a list: the list shows as it is in the page.
Ctrl+K preview of a page with a callout: the callout keeps its color and kind.
Ctrl+K preview of a page with a table (a list in a page): its first rows.
Recents replaces Today in the side list: the last 8 pages opened, newest first, above Pinned, Folders, Pages.
/list makes a list in a page: pages that match a line, in a Table by default, with the view and Filters above it.
The view menu of a list in a page: Table, List, Gallery, Board (Calendar and Timeline later); group by folder or callout kind.
List view: one quiet line per page, its folder's dot and when it was edited.
Gallery view: a card per page, its first lines as the preview.
Board view, grouped by folder: a column per folder; dragging a card to another column moves the page there.
Floating tab: the page floats over the reader at 560 px; the column keeps a 24 px margin and the gutter fits inside.
Narrow pane: 460 px beside the reader; the handle sits inside the margin; menus stay inside the pane.
Phone: the page at 390 px; every menu is a bottom sheet with the same search, groups and rows.
